description: Three stereo send-and-return loops, each adding a delayed copy of what comes back to the signal at IN

params.text: Sets how much of that channel's delayed ARRIVALS signal is added to its DEPARTURES output, silence at the left and full at the right
Sets how far back in that channel's memory the ARRIVALS signal is read from, 0 to 3 seconds
Clears that channel's delay memory and drops its DEPARTURES output to 0V; the button is momentary and acts on the frame it is pressed

inputs.text: The left half of the source signal, added undelayed to the left DEPARTURES output of all three channels
The right half of the source signal, added undelayed to the right DEPARTURES output of all three channels
The left return for that channel, written into its delay memory and read back after the DELAY time
The right return for that channel, written into its delay memory and read back after the DELAY time
Added to that channel's GAIN knob at 10% per volt, with the total clamped between silence and full
Added to that channel's DELAY knob at 0.3 seconds per volt; the total is clamped at 0 but not at 3 seconds, so a large CV reads a wrong place in the memory rather than stopping at the longest delay

outputs.text: The left IN signal plus that channel's delayed left ARRIVALS signal scaled by GAIN
The right IN signal plus that channel's delayed right ARRIVALS signal scaled by GAIN

notes: a channel does nothing on its own: patch its DEPARTURES pair out to an effect chain and that chain back into its ARRIVALS pair, or the departure output carries the IN signal alone.
there is no clipper anywhere in the module, so a loop with gain added in the chain can build without limit.
the delay memory is 3 seconds long, sized from the sample rate when the module is added; change the engine sample rate afterwards and the delay times are wrong until the module is replaced.
